objective: Make release eligibility a property of the evidence rather than of a summary file: bind each run to a provenance record over its event log and scenario manifest, require an attributable and complete human audit, and share one predicate between the runner, the metrics collector, the report and an independent checker.
decision_supported: Can a scripted run, an edited log, a swapped manifest or an unattributed audit be published as release evidence, or does every stage agree to refuse it and name the input that disagreed?
acceptance: one predicate in tools/scripts/release_eligibility.py decides eligibility and is used by the runner, the metrics collector and the release report
eligibility binds the source commit, the runner identity, the environment, the per-run seed, the scenario, the event-log content hash and the scenario-manifest hash
a scripted run can never be release-eligible, including when the summary claims otherwise
a hand-written or copied summary.json cannot grant eligibility
an edited event log and a changed scenario manifest are each refused by content hash
a provenance record with an unsupported format or version is refused rather than partially trusted
the human audit must name a reviewer, a timestamp and a per-run oracle status, and must cover every run
a run that claims completion while its audited oracle status disagrees is reported as a false completion
a summary that claims eligibility the evidence does not support is itself reported as a finding
metrics and the release report share the predicate, so they cannot disagree about the same run
check_evaluation_eligibility.py re-checks a run directory independently, exits non-zero when refused, and never repairs an input
the refusal reasons are stable strings and the documentation tabulates each one
the manifest is bound by recorded path, so a verifier checks the file the runner hashed rather than a different file that shares a scenario_id
evidence: Task Packet schema validation output with exit code
targeted pytest output listing the collected Issue #82 test names, pass counts and exit codes

before-fix reproduction: a scripted log beside a hand-written summary claiming runner=external and release_eligible=true was accepted and reported runner=external; after the fix the same directory is refused with the scripted-runner reason
mutation probe 1 output: with the event-log hash comparison disabled, the two edited-log tests fail
mutation probe 2 output: with the scripted-runner rejection disabled, the scripted-runner test fails
mutation probe 3 output: with the reviewer and timestamp check disabled, four audit-attribution tests fail
end-to-end runner output showing provenance.json written with per-run log and manifest hashes and summary.json carrying release_eligible false with named reasons for a scripted run
checker output for an eligible external run exiting 0 with no reasons, and for the same run after one event was edited exiting 1 with the log-hash reason
make test, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check, make context-check, make evaluation-check and make docs output with exit codes
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
stop_conditions: Eligibility is still decided by a value that a person can type into summary.json.
A scripted run reaches an eligible verdict through any path.
Making the gate fail closed requires changing interfaces/, libs/contracts/ or any runtime service.
The checker repairs, rewrites or deletes an input instead of refusing it.
The gate is claimed to be a signature or an attestation rather than a content hash recorded by an approval step.
data_classification: internal; tests use temporary directories and the checked-in frozen scenario manifest, and commit no evaluation evidence
model_policy: no model call; eligibility is a deterministic recomputation over committed inputs
risks_and_fallbacks: A tighter gate could block a legitimate release. The eligibility checker prints every reason and the manual run path is documented, so a refusal is diagnosable rather than a dead end.
A content hash is not a signature. The documentation states this limit and points at signing as a deployment decision instead of implying attestation.

Requiring a timestamp and reviewer could stall an urgent decision. The audit format is a small JSON object, and an incomplete audit is refused rather than silently downgraded, which is the point of the control.
Binding the manifest by path could break when the tree moves. Paths are recorded relative to the repository when possible with an absolute fallback, and a missing manifest is a named refusal.
